top_choice_rationale: The lattice clock rests on a distinct invention, the magic-wavelength condition that cancels the trap light shift so many neutral atoms can be held in the Lamb-Dicke regime, which is neither the 2005 comb nor the 2012 single-system control. It has been reproduced independently in Sr, Yb and Hg and compared between laboratories near 1e-18, so it is mature. The two-name allocation (Katori for the concept, Ye for the many-atom architecture at record performance) is defensible if the citation stays confined to the lattice clock; the exclusion of Takamoto, Ido and Lemonde is a real cost but does not make no award preferable.
